title: Back Bay skyline across the Charles River (the classic Boston postcard)
note: Hancock Tower and the Prudential must dominate; the Charles fills the foreground.

title: Financial District & waterfront from Boston Harbor
note: Custom House Tower, One International Place, harbour wharves.

title: Eye level on Boston Common, looking to the State House
note: Street realism: path surface, benches, people, tree canopy overhead, the gold dome beyond.

title: Low oblique over the Back Bay grid
note: Rowhouse rhythm, brick and brownstone variation, Commonwealth Ave mall.

title: Zakim Bunker Hill Bridge from the north
note: The inverted-Y towers and cable fan must be unmistakable.

title: Seaport / Fort Point at night
note: Window lights, street lamps, reflections on the channel, bloom discipline.

title: High aerial over the whole peninsula
note: Overall city read: land/water shape, density gradient, colour variety.

title: Fenway Park and the Emerald Necklace
note: The ballpark bowl, light towers and the Green Monster. The viewpoint used to face north-east at the Charles, which is not where Fenway Park is.

title: State House golden dome over Beacon Hill
note: Gilded dome specular response, brick rowhouse texture, warm low sun.

title: Low over the Charles basin toward Back Bay
note: Water close-up: wave detail, reflections of the Back Bay skyline, shoreline foam.

title: Boston Harbor looking back at the Financial District
note: Open-water swell, turbid green-brown colour, wharves and the shoreline transition.

title: Commonwealth Avenue Mall at eye level
note: Street trees in rows down the mall, brownstone frontage, moving traffic and people. The viewpoint used to sit in a service yard three blocks away.

title: Downtown intersection, pedestrian level
note: Vehicles, crossings, lane markings, kerbs and footfall in the Financial District.

title: Downtown at street level after dark
note: Street lamps, shopfronts, headlights and wet-looking tarmac. The only eye-level night test: every emissive in the city is authored display-referred and has to survive the exposure lift.

title: The Prudential Tower and its podium from the south-west
note: Landmark-vs-OSM overlap: the hand-authored tower has to sit in its podium, not through the buildings around it.

title: Boylston Street below the Prudential
note: Looking up the tower from the street; any footprint intersecting the mesh shows here first.

title: Copley Square: Trinity Church and the Boston Public Library
note: Two hand-authored landmark meshes side by side. If either one's OSM footprint is not suppressed, it shows here as a second building in the same place.

title: Back Bay rowhouse roofs, close
note: Party walls and roof planes at close range. Adjacent rowhouses are traced separately in OpenStreetMap, so their shared wall is two coincident quads and their roofs meet in overlapping slivers; this is where that shows.

title: USS Constitution at the Charlestown Navy Yard
note: Three masts, yards, standing rigging, black-and-white hull, the granite pier and Dry Dock 1. The oldest commissioned warship afloat; it has to read as a ship, not a hull with poles.

title: Charlestown Navy Yard from the harbour
note: The Constitution, the yard's brick storehouses and Bunker Hill Monument behind.

title: Harvard Yard from the south
note: Widener's colonnade, Memorial Church's spire, the Yard's brick and the trees over it.

title: MIT across Killian Court
note: The Great Dome on axis over Killian Court, the limestone wings, and the Charles behind the camera.

title: Northeastern University on Huntington Avenue
note: Snell Library's glass drum, the quad, Huntington Avenue and the Green Line reservation.

title: Charles River surface, close
note: Wave shape, foam, glitter and turbidity at the distance a person actually stands from water.

title: Flags on the Financial District
note: American flags on facades and roofs, hanging and flying, at a size you can read.

title: 125 High Street from the south-west
note: The worst remaining footprint interpenetration: a 100 m building:part crossing the walls of the 90 m relation it belongs to.

title: The State House south front, close
note: Landmark facade detail at conversational distance: does the brick have windows in it, or is it a blank mass with invisible recessed reveals?

title: The view a visitor lands on
note: The application's own opening framing and hour, the first thing a visitor sees. Looks south-east down the Charles with the sun behind: shoot it with qa/boot-shot.mjs to photograph the real default, since __debug.setView replaces it.

title: The opening framing at mid-morning
note: The opening framing with the sun in the east instead of behind the camera, as a check that the composition does not depend on the hour.

title: Boston Air Traffic Control Tower across the Logan airfield
note: The tower must read as a low base, a long slender battered shaft and a glazed cab flaring out past it — not a full-width concrete slab. Cab and mast must appear exactly once.

title: Oblique aerial down Logan runway 04R/22L
note: Threshold, touchdown zone and centreline markings, and the pavement tone against the infield grass.

title: Logan apron, taxi route and threshold together
note: The wide read of the airfield: apron, taxiways and runway in one frame, where pale patches show up.
